transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I’ve gotten so strict about cutting back how much I eat that I hardly feel like I’m taking in anything at all anymore. It started as a way to stay disciplined, but now it feels like I've just gone too far with it.
Do you ever experience episodes where you feel you've lost control and eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No, I never have times where I lose control or eat a large amount of food. My focus is entirely on strictly cutting back and restricting what I eat.
To help me understand better, have you lost a significant amount of weight, and is your current weight below what is typically expected for your height?

Yes, I've lost quite a bit of weight and my clothes are hanging off me now, to the point where a doctor told me my weight is too low. Honestly, I think everyone is overreacting because seeing the scale go down just makes me feel like I’m finally doing something right.
Have you experienced physical changes like your menstrual periods stopping, or if you are male, a significant loss of interest in sex?
I haven't really noticed or paid much attention to that, to be honest. I've been so focused on my routine and trying to keep my energy up for work that I haven't even thought about it.
To help me clarify, if you are female, have your menstrual periods stopped or become irregular? If you are male, have you noticed a significant drop in your sexual drive?
I honestly haven't been paying attention to my periods, so I'm not really sure if they've changed or stopped. My mind has been so focused on my weight and work that I just haven't kept track of it.
Do you experience an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though others have told you that your weight is already too low?

Yes, I get absolutely panicky if the scale goes up even half a pound because I worry everyone at the warehouse will see me as lazy and unprofessional. Even though the doctor says my weight is too low, I honestly think they are overreacting, and hearing that I look tiny actually makes me feel like I'm finally doing something right.
Could you share your current height and weight with me, as well as how much weight you have lost recently?

I don't really know my exact height or weight off the top of my head, and I'm not sure exactly how many pounds I've lost. I just know that my clothes are hanging off me now and people at work and church keep saying I look very small.
Even if you haven't been keeping close track, do you remember roughly when you had your last menstrual period, or if you've had one at all in the last three months?

I honestly can't remember, and I'm really not sure if I've had one in the last three months. I've just been so focused on my routine and trying to keep my energy up for work that I haven't paid any attention to it.
Besides restricting your food intake, do you use other methods to control your weight, such as exercising excessively, making yourself throw up, or using laxatives or diet pills?
No, I don't do any of those things. I've never used laxatives, made myself throw up, taken diet pills, or exercised excessively. I only control my weight by strictly restricting how much food I eat.
Since you mentioned tracking the scale closely and worrying about even a half-pound increase, what was the weight on the scale the last time you stepped on it?
I don't remember the exact number on the scale from the last time I stepped on it. I try not to focus too much on the specific number itself, I just get really anxious if I see it go up at all.
When you look in the mirror, do you perceive yourself as overweight or feel that certain parts of your body are too big, even though others tell you that you are very thin?

Yes, when I look in the mirror at home or in the locker room, all I can see are my stomach and thighs looking too big. Even though others say I look tiny, seeing those parts makes me feel like I'm not disciplined enough, which just reminds me of why I was passed over for that promotion. I feel like I have to stay as small as possible to be worth anything.
When your doctor told you that your weight was too low, did they happen to mention your specific weight, BMI, or how much underweight you are?
I don't remember the exact weight or BMI numbers they mentioned. I didn't really pay much attention to it because I felt like they were just overreacting anyway.
What was your typical weight before you started strictly restricting your food, or what clothing size did you wear back then compared to now?
I don't really remember my exact weight or what specific clothing sizes I used to wear before. I just know that my current clothes are noticeably hanging off me now and feel way too big.
Have you noticed other physical changes, like feeling constantly cold even when it's warm, or having dizzy spells when you stand up?

I haven't really noticed feeling constantly cold, but I've definitely had some bad dizziness and even nearly fainted on the warehouse floor. I feel pretty drained lately, but I still think I'm mostly fine as long as I just push through the tiredness.
